key_insight: A qubit-efficient shell-model mapping can make VQE practical for nuclear ground-state calculations while preserving useful wavefunction fidelity.
engineering_relevance: The work shows how mapping choice strongly affects qubit count, circuit complexity, and hardware performance, which is critical for scaling quantum algorithms to larger nuclei.
method: Compared three qubit-mapping strategies for the nuclear shell model: SD, cSD, and pnSD.
Ran VQE circuits up to 26 qubits for $^{10}$B and $^{12}$C on a noisy simulator and IBM quantum hardware.
Used post-error mitigation and compared energies and wavefunction fidelity against exact shell-model results.
evidence_signal: For $^{10}$B, the best hardware result was SD mapping with 0.21% error, while cSD and pnSD gave 3.37% and 8.88%; for $^{12}$C with cSD, the mitigated result was 6.82% from exact.
watch_item: Performance depends strongly on the chosen mapping and error mitigation, so hardware results may not generalize without careful calibration and resource trade-off analysis.
paper_title: Qubit-efficient variational algorithm for nuclear structure
